content: The pharmacodynamic interaction between bacteriostatic agents and bactericidal agents, such as ceftriaxone, may reduce the effectiveness of the latter. Caution and monitoring are advised when these agents are co-administered. Similarly, erythromycin ethylsuccinate can decrease the effects of cefuroxime through pharmacodynamic antagonism, necessitating careful monitoring. Cenobamate reduces the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended, including dose increases of CYP3A4 substrates when co-administered with cenobamate. Conversely, erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases ceritinib levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) inhibition, requiring caution and monitoring. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate also increases the levels or effects of cevimeline by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating caution. Co-administration with chloroquine or ciprofloxacin, both of which prolong the QTc interval, increases the risk of QTc-related toxicity, including torsades de pointes, particularly in predisposed patients. ECG monitoring is recommended in such cases. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate raises citalopram levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, which may increase the risk of QTc prolongation. ECG monitoring is advised when co-administered with drugs that prolong the QT interval. Similarly, erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases clarithromycin and conivaptan levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, requiring caution and monitoring. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate decreases the levels of conjugated estrogens (oral forms) by altering intestinal flora, though the risk of contraceptive failure is low. However, it increases the levels of conjugated estrogens (oral and vaginal forms) and cortisone via P-glycoprotein inhibition, necessitating monitoring. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases crizotinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein transport. Dose reductions of co-administered CYP3A4 substrates may be necessary. ECG monitoring is recommended due to the potential for QTc prolongation. Crofelemer, which inhibits CYP3A4 and certain transporters in the gut, increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels, requiring therapy adjustments and close monitoring. Cyclosporine levels are increased by erythromycin ethylsuccinate via P-glycoprotein inhibition, and vice versa, necessitating caution. Similarly, erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases dabigatran levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition, and co-administration should be avoided in patients with reduced renal function (CrCl <30 mL/min for atrial fibrillation or <50 mL/min for DVT/PE treatment). Dabrafenib decreases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring therapy adjustments. Conversely, erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases dactinomycin levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition, necessitating caution. Danazol and danicopan also increase erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels through CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein inhibition, respectively, requiring monitoring and potential dose adjustments. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases dapsone and daridorexant levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Daridorexant doses should not exceed 25 mg per night when co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Similarly, erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases darunavir levels, necessitating close monitoring and therapy adjustments. Dasatinib and erythromycin ethylsuccinate both prolong the QTc interval, requiring close monitoring. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases daunorubicin levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition, necessitating caution. Deferasirox decreases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring monitoring. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases deflazacort levels via CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein inhibition, necessitating close monitoring. Deutetrabenazine and erythromycin ethylsuccinate both prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of torsades de pointes under certain conditions. ECG monitoring is recommended. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases dexamethasone and diazepam levels via P-glycoprotein and CYP3A4 inhibition, respectively. Therapy adjustments may be required to mitigate adverse effects. Similarly, erythromycin ethylsuccinate decreases dienogest/estradiol valerate levels by altering intestinal flora, though the risk of contraceptive failure is low. Monitoring for adverse effects such as nausea and irregular bleeding is recommended. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases digoxin and disopyramide levels via P-glycoprotein and CYP3A4 inhibition, respectively, necessitating caution. It also increases docetaxel levels via both mechanisms, requiring monitoring. Dolasetron and erythromycin ethylsuccinate both prolong the QTc interval, necessitating therapy adjustments. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases donepezil and doxorubicin levels via CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein inhibition, requiring caution. It also increases dutasteride levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, necessitating monitoring. Duvelisib increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4, requiring therapy adjustments to mitigate toxicity risks. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases efavirenz levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, necessitating caution. Elagolix, a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer, affects erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels, requiring close monitoring. Eliglustat increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition, necessitating therapy adjustments. Eluxadoline increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels by reducing metabolism, requiring caution. Similarly, elvitegravir/cobicistat increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, necessitating close monitoring. Cobicistat is contraindicated with CYP3A4 substrates associated with serious adverse events. Encorafenib, which both inhibits and induces CYP3A4, increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels, requiring close monitoring. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases eplerenone and erlotinib levels via CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein inhibition, respectively, necessitating caution. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate decreases estradiol and other estrogens' levels by altering intestinal flora, though the risk of contraceptive failure is low. It increases their levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition, requiring monitoring. Eszopiclone levels are increased by erythromycin ethylsuccinate through enhanced absorption and CYP3A4 inhibition, necessitating dose reductions. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases etoposide levels via CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein inhibition, requiring caution. It also increases eucalyptus and exemestane levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, necessitating monitoring. Ezogabine and erythromycin ethylsuccinate both prolong the QTc interval, requiring ECG monitoring. Fedratinib increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, necessitating dose adjustments. Similarly, erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases finasteride and finerenone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, requiring close monitoring. Finerenone dosage adjustments may be necessary based on serum potassium levels. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and flecainide both prolong the QTc interval, requiring close monitoring. It increases fludrocortisone levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition, necessitating caution. Fluoxetine and erythromycin ethylsuccinate both prolong the QTc interval, requiring therapy adjustments. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases fluvastatin toxicity, potentially increasing the risk of myopathy. Fluvoxamine and erythromycin ethylsuccinate both prolong the QTc interval, requiring close monitoring. Foscarnet and erythromycin ethylsuccinate also prolong the QTc interval, necessitating therapy adjustments. Fostamatinib increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition, requiring monitoring for toxicities. Fostemsavir, which inhibits OATP1B1/3 transporters, increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels and prolongs the QTc interval, necessitating caution. Gadobenate and erythromycin ethylsuccinate both prolong the QTc interval, requiring monitoring. Similarly, gemtuzumab and erythromycin ethylsuccinate increase the QTc interval, necessitating caution. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases gentamicin levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition, requiring monitoring. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases gepirone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition and prolongs the QTc interval, necessitating therapy adjustments. Goserelin increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval, increasing the risk of torsades de pointes. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases guanfacine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, requiring dose reductions for extended-release formulations. Histrelin increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval, necessitating caution. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases hydrocortisone levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition, requiring monitoring. Hydroxyzine increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval, necessitating caution.
